title.narrative: Strengthening policy and performance-oriented PFM systems in Mongolia

description.narrative: The proposed Joint Programme (JP) on Strengthening Policy and Performance-Oriented PublicFinancial Management (PFM) Systems in Mongolia is designed to address critical structural gaps inMongolias fiscal governance system. Building on prior reforms supported by the European Union andpartners, including the EU-funded SDG-aligned budgeting programme, the JP responds to persistentchallenges in fiscal risk management, medium-term budgeting, domestic revenue mobilization, andperformance-based expenditure management. These gaps continue to constrain the Governmentsability to align public resources with national development priorities, including Vision 2050, the FiveYearDevelopment Guidelines (2026-2030), and the SDGs.The rationale of the programme is grounded in both national demand and demonstrated reformneeds. Previous interventions have successfully introduced results-based budgeting (RBB) andplanning frameworks; however, systemic weaknesses remain in fiscal risk analysis, integration of policyand budgeting cycles, and performance monitoring. For example, Mongolia currently lacks acomprehensive methodology for fiscal risk assessment within the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework,limiting the robustness of fiscal planning and stability. The JP therefore aims to institutionalize thesereforms and move from piloting to full system-wide implementation.
